album: Do You Love the Color of the Sky?
label: Polyvinyl Records
release_notes: Recent album from Los Angeles band Dummy, their first for Polyvinyl. Earlier records: debut Mandatory Enjoyment (2021), Free Energy (2024) and the remix album Bubbelibrium DLC (2025). Built from the band's own recorded sample library, chopped up and reassembled, with guitars pushed back (Northern Transmissions, Treble).

Emma Maatman - keyboards, vocals; Nathan O'Dell - guitar, vocals; Joe Trainor - guitar (also a publicist); Alex Ewell - drums, vocals; Lance Umble - bass. Guests: Nina Pitchkites ("Song of Mana"); Allyson Foster and Paul Benson of New Issue ("Alluvial Fan").

Produced, recorded and mixed by Dummy and Joo-Joo Ashworth, in a home studio and at Studio 22, Los Angeles. Ashworth also made Dummy's Mandatory Enjoyment there (Discogs) and has produced Froth and Holy Wave records. Mastered by Mikey Young of Eddy Current Suppression Ring and Total Control.

The band says the songs take on climate degradation, A.I. and the devaluation of art, and the surveillance state (Polyvinyl). Label comparisons: Seefeel, Disco Inferno, early Bjork, Madonna's Ray of Light.

pull_quotes.text: a softly-lit and pastel-hued otherland easy to get lost in
sonically disorienting but also incredibly cohesive

draft_comment: Dreamy, drone-flecked, breakbeat-driven indie electronica from L.A., with critics reaching for Seefeel, Broadcast and Stereolab. Two FCC tracks late in the sequence (9 and 10).

tracks.title: April Limousine
tracks.notes: Stuttering psychedelic breakbeat that melts into a slow, ethereal float, with little recognizable guitar (Treble, Northern Transmissions). Minimal and repetitive, Emma Maatman's vocals used like another instrument, building to a climactic coda (Clash, Treble).

tracks.title: Alluvial Fan
tracks.notes: Funky, slacker-ish mood piece (Stereogum). Precise guitar and drum rhythm, shared vocals from Maatman, Ewell and O'Dell, plus guest vocals from Allyson Foster and Paul Benson of New Issue (AudioFuzz).

tracks.title: Full Spectrum Dominance
tracks.notes: Wobbling wah-wah guitar and a lumbering, baggy bassline (Northern Transmissions, Treble), like Stereolab remixed by Lemon Jelly (Line of Best Fit). Pulls back to a heartbeat pulse, breaks down into distorted guitar, then settles to a steady groove that leads into the next track (Clash).

tracks.title: Squeaky Wheel
tracks.notes: Long, repetitive and textural, spiralling upward around layered Maatman vocals (Northern Transmissions, Treble). Hectic but inviting (Glide).

tracks.title: Touch the Perfect Speed
tracks.notes: Keeps a strong rhythmic emphasis inside hazier textures (AudioFuzz).

tracks.title: Song of Mana
tracks.notes: Starts as a wistful ambient-pop drift, then hardens into acid-techno squelch (Northern Transmissions, Treble). Gently angular synths and cryptic vocals, a strange video-game-soundtrack feel (Line of Best Fit). Guest vocals: Nina Pitchkites.

tracks.title: Omen Globe
tracks.notes: Short, strobing, dizzy rush of ravey shoegaze (Treble, Northern Transmissions). Punk-tinted (Glide).

tracks.title: C.B.B.S.I.M.M.P.W.M.
tracks.notes: Instrumental (wordless on Genius; Clash says the band lean into the instrumental side). Short, works as a breather between louder tracks (AudioFuzz).

tracks.title: N of 1
tracks.notes: Locks onto a single groove with huge drums and smeared guitar drones, glacial guitar cut into a jungle-inspired drum setting (Line of Best Fit, AudioFuzz). Sticky, dancefloor-ready feel (Line of Best Fit).

tracks.title: Heaven's What You Make of It
tracks.notes: Pace: check (BPM source says ~164 BPM, but critics call it restrained). Driven by an infectious bassline with strong Maatman vocals (Treble). Opens and closes like a portal, with reversed synths and rippling beats (Line of Best Fit). Closer.
